If aqueous solution of the electrolyte boils at 375 K and $K_b$ for water is $0.52\,\mathrm{K\,kg\,mol}^{-1}$, then the mole fraction of the electrolyte solute $(x_2)$ in the solution can be expressed as
(Given : density of water $=1\,\mathrm{g/mL}$ and boiling point of water $=373\,\mathrm{K}$ )
questions.solution:
Relative lowering of vapour pressure for an electrolyte: $\frac{p^\circ-p_s}{p^\circ}=i\,x_2$
$\frac{640-600}{640}=\frac{1}{16}$, so $i\,x_2=\frac{1}{16}$ ...(1)
Boiling-point elevation: $\Delta T_b=i\,K_b\,m$, where $\Delta T_b=375-373=2\ \text{K}$
Mass of water $=100\ \text{g}=0.1\ \text{kg}$, so $m=\frac{W/M}{0.1}=\frac{10W}{M}\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$
$2=i\times0.52\times\frac{10W}{M}$, which gives $i=\frac{2M}{5.2W}=\frac{M}{2.6W}$
From (1): $x_2=\frac{1}{16i}=\frac{2.6}{16}\times\frac{W}{M}=\frac{1.3}{8}\times\frac{W}{M}$
Answer: (D) $\frac{1.3}{8}\times\frac{W}{M}$

Statement II : Mixture of methanol and $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ shows positive deviation deviation from Raoult's law.
